title: Finite etale-origin site comparison preserves the exceptional base-change mate
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient data of [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ has characteristic $p_0$, $\ell\ne p_0$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, $n\geq1$, and $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $X,Y,Y'$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y'\to Y$ be $k$-morphisms, with $f$ separated of finite type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Form the Cartesian square [def-cbc-compact-support-square] with $X'=X\times_Y Y'$, $g_X:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$. Choose a compactification $c=(j,r)$, $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{r}Y$, with $j$ open and $r$ proper, and its pullback $c'=(j',r')$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Assume that $\overline X$ and $\overline X'=\overline X\times_Y Y'$ are finite-type $k$-schemes and that $\dim\overline X\leq d$, $\dim\overline X'\leq d'$ for integers $d,d'\geq0$, with dimension as in [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension].

Use ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $C_T=\nu_T^*$ for exact derived comparison pullback [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback]. Put $F=Rr_{\mathrm{et},*}j_!^{\mathrm{et}}$, $F'=Rr'_{\mathrm{et},*}j'_!^{\mathrm{et}}$, using [def-amb-etale-compact-support], and let $R=f_c^\times$, $R'=f_{c'}'^\times$ be their ordinary etale right adjoints [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], with counits $\epsilon^e,\epsilon'^e$. Put $P=Rf_!^c$, $P'=Rf'_!^{c'}$ for pro-etale compact supports [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], and $H=C_XR R\nu_{Y,*}$, $H'=C_{X'}R'R\nu_{Y',*}$ for the finite exceptional functors [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], with the bounded-below etale-origin Hom bijections of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class]. Here the relative Hom bijections are the specified transported ones, with the following normalization, rather than arbitrary natural bijections. Put $U_T=R\nu_{T,*}$ and let $a_G:PC_XG\xrightarrow{\sim}C_YFG$ be [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] for the identity witness. Explicitly, $a_G=C_{c,G}^{-1}$, where $C_{c,G}:C_YFG\xrightarrow{\sim}PC_XG$ is the canonical proper-and-open comparison for the chosen compactification in [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison]; the primed $a'$ is $C_{c'}^{-1}$ in the same way. Write $J$ for the ordinary $F\dashv R$ Hom bijection and $\eta$ for the comparison unit. For $G\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $N\in D^+(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ the relative bijection is the composite
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}(PC_XG,N)&\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(C_YFG,N)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(FG,U_YN)\\
&\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(G,RU_YN)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(C_XG,C_XRU_YN),
\end{aligned}$$
where the arrows send $z$ to $z a_G^{-1}$, then to $U_Y(z a_G^{-1})\eta_{FG}$, then apply $J$, then apply $C_X$. All these objects lie in the stated bounded-below domains. On a witness $\alpha:C_XG\xrightarrow{\sim}K$, first precompose with $P\alpha$ and finally precompose with $\alpha^{-1}$. Use the identical normalization with primes for $P',H'$. This is the Hom-chain construction of the cited relative adjunction, not an adjunction on the entire pro-etale category.

For every morphism $u:T'\to T$ write
$$\kappa_u:C_{T'}u_{\mathrm{et}}^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lu_{\mathrm{proet}}^*C_T$$
for the canonical inverse-image comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. For $L\in D^+(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, let
$$h_{f,L}:C_XRL\xrightarrow{\sim}HC_YL$$
be $C_XR$ applied to the site-comparison unit $L\xrightarrow{\sim}R\nu_{Y,*}C_YL$ of [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]; define $h_{f',-}$ in the same way.

Let $B^e:g_{\mathrm{et}}^*F\xrightarrow{\sim}F'g_{X,\mathrm{et}}^*$ be the compact-support exchange of [def-cbc-exchange-map, thm-cbc-finite-torsion] and $B^p:Lg_{\mathrm{proet}}^*P\xrightarrow{\sim}P'Lg_{X,\mathrm{proet}}^*$ its transported exchange on bounded-below etale-origin inputs [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale]. For the chosen $c,c'$, the compactification formula in [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale] gives the transported exchange on $C_XG$ as
$B^p_{C_XG}=T^c_G\circ C_{Y'}(B^e_G)\circ(S^c_G)^{-1}$,
where $S^c_G=Lg_{\mathrm{proet}}^*(C_{c,G})\circ\kappa_{g,FG}$ and $T^c_G=P'(\kappa_{g_X,G})\circ C_{c',g_{X,\mathrm{et}}^*G}$; on a witnessed input it is conjugated by the witness. Let $\beta^e_L:g_{X,\mathrm{et}}^*RL\to R'g_{\mathrm{et}}^*L$ be the $F'\dashv R'$ transpose of
$$g_{\mathrm{et}}^*(\epsilon^e_L)\circ(B^e_{RL})^{-1}.$$
Let $\epsilon^p_{C_YL}:PHC_YL\to C_YL$ be the map corresponding to $1_{HC_YL}$ under the relative Hom bijection for $P,H$. Define $\beta^p_{C_YL}:Lg_{X,\mathrm{proet}}^*HC_YL\to H'Lg_{\mathrm{proet}}^*C_YL$ to be the relative $P',H'$ transpose of
$$Lg_{\mathrm{proet}}^*(\epsilon^p_{C_YL})\circ(B^p_{HC_YL})^{-1}.$$
These are the counit-transpose mates of inverse compact-support exchange, as in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. All inputs in these formulas are bounded below and, when required as source inputs of the relative Hom bijections, of etale origin.

Define the endpoint isomorphisms
$$v_L=\kappa_{g_X,RL}^{-1}\circ Lg_{X,\mathrm{proet}}^*(h_{f,L}^{-1}):Lg_{X,\mathrm{proet}}^*HC_YL\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{X'}g_{X,\mathrm{et}}^*RL,$$
$$w_L=h_{f',g_{\mathrm{et}}^*L}^{-1}\circ H'(\kappa_{g,L}^{-1}):H'Lg_{\mathrm{proet}}^*C_YL\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{X'}R'g_{\mathrm{et}}^*L.$$
Then the actual exceptional mates satisfy
$$w_L\circ\beta^p_{C_YL}=C_{X'}(\beta^e_L)\circ v_L.$$
The equality is natural in $L$ and is preserved by replacing $C_YL$ with an isomorphic witnessed input. No isomorphy of $\beta^e$ or $\beta^p$, smoothness of $f$, or unrestricted pro-etale adjunction is assumed.

proof.text: Write $s=g_{\mathrm{et}}^*$, $t=g_{X,\mathrm{et}}^*$, $S=Lg_{\mathrm{proet}}^*$ and $T=Lg_{X,\mathrm{proet}}^*$. The two compactifications and their dimension bounds satisfy the hypotheses of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] separately, with bounds $d$ and $d'$. Thus the relative Hom bijections are natural and injective on every source used here. Their source objects have the exhibited witnesses: $HC_YL$ is isomorphic to $C_XRL$ by $h_{f,L}$, and $THC_YL$ is isomorphic to $C_{X'}tRL$ by $Th_{f,L}\circ\kappa_{g_X,RL}$. The assumed bounded-below conditions put $RL,tRL,sL,R'sL$ and every Hom-chain argument in the domain of the fully faithful comparison of [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]. No assertion about unrestricted pro-etale adjunctions is used.

source.place: Actual-adjoint comparison and final base-change sentences; explicit counit-transpose calculation.

proof.text:
Let $\Psi$ be the normalized relative bijection in the statement. If $b:FG\to M$ is an etale morphism, substitution of $z=C_Y(b)\circ a_G$ in that chain gives $U_YC_Y(b)\circ\eta_{FG}=\eta_M\circ b$, by naturality of the unit [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]. Naturality of the ordinary adjunction bijection $J$ in its target gives $J(\eta_M\circ b)=R(\eta_M)\circ J(b)$. Consequently
$$\Psi_{C_XG,C_YM}(C_Y(b)\circ a_G)=h_{f,M}\circ C_X(J(b)).$$
Here $a_G$ is precisely the natural isomorphism of [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison]; no unnamed comparison replaces it. Repeat this calculation with primes to obtain the same formula for $\Psi'$. This is an expansion of the chosen Hom-chain definition using the ordinary adjunction of [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint].

source.place: Actual-adjoint comparison and final base-change sentences; explicit counit-transpose calculation.

proof.text:
Put $h=h_{f,L}$ and abbreviate $\epsilon^e_L=e$, $\epsilon^p_{C_YL}=E$. In Step 2 take $G=RL$ and $b=e$. The ordinary transpose of its counit is $1_{RL}$, so $\Psi(C_Y(e)\circ a_{RL})=h$. By the definition of $E$, $\Psi(E)=1_{HC_YL}$; naturality in the witnessed source from [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] gives $\Psi(E\circ P(h))=h$. Injectivity therefore yields the required normalization of the actual counit:
$$E\circ P(h)=C_Y(e)\circ a_{RL}.$$
Only naturality and injectivity of the stated relative Hom bijection are used. The ordinary counit-transpose convention is the one in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate].

source.place: Actual-adjoint comparison and final base-change sentences; explicit counit-transpose calculation.

proof.text:
For an etale $G$ put $k_G=\kappa_{g_X,G}$ and $l_M=\kappa_{g,M}$. Let $a'$ denote the primed compact-support comparison. By the compactification clause of [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale], the exchange on the chosen $c,c'$ is the transported compactification exchange. Substituting $C_{c,G}=a_G^{-1}$, $C_{c',tG}=a'^{-1}_{tG}$ (the normalization of [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] fixed in the statement) and the pullback comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] gives $B^p_{C_XG}=P'(k_G)(a'_{tG})^{-1}C_{Y'}(B^e_G)l_{FG}^{-1}S(a_G)$, that is,
$$a'_{tG}\circ P'(k_G^{-1})\circ B^p_{C_XG}=C_{Y'}(B^e_G)\circ l_{FG}^{-1}\circ S(a_G).$$
All factors are isomorphisms on these inputs ($B^e_G$ by [thm-cbc-finite-torsion]; $j$ is quasi-compact because $X$ is Noetherian); inverting and rearranging gives
$$(B^p_{C_XG})^{-1}\circ P'(k_G)\circ(a'_{tG})^{-1}=S(a_G^{-1})\circ l_{FG}\circ C_{Y'}((B^e_G)^{-1}).$$
This just writes out the definition of transport and cancels inverse factors; it does not assert isomorphy of either exceptional mate.

source.place: Actual-adjoint comparison and final base-change sentences; explicit counit-transpose calculation.

proof.text:
Set $Q=T(h)\circ k_{RL}=v_L^{-1}$,
$$z^p=S(E)\circ(B^p_{HC_YL})^{-1},\qquad z^e=s(e)\circ(B^e_{RL})^{-1}.$$
Naturality of $B^p$ at $h$ says
$$(B^p_{HC_YL})^{-1}P'(Th)=S(P h)(B^p_{C_XRL})^{-1}.$$
Use this equation, Step 3, and Step 4 with $G=RL$ in turn. Functoriality and cancellation give
$$\begin{aligned}
z^pP'(Q)(a'_{tRL})^{-1}
&=S(EP h)(B^p_{C_XRL})^{-1}P'(k_{RL})(a'_{tRL})^{-1}\\
&=S(C_Y(e)a_{RL})S(a_{RL}^{-1})l_{FRL}C_{Y'}((B^e_{RL})^{-1})\\
&=S(C_Y(e))l_{FRL}C_{Y'}((B^e_{RL})^{-1})\\
&=l_L C_{Y'}(s(e)(B^e_{RL})^{-1})=l_L C_{Y'}(z^e).
\end{aligned}$$
The penultimate equality is exactly naturality of $\kappa_g$ at $e$. The displayed naturality equation at $h$ is the witness clause of [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale]: $HC_YL$ carries the witness $(RL,h)$, so by that statement $B^p_{HC_YL}=P'(Th)\circ B^p_{C_XRL}\circ S(Ph)^{-1}$, which is the equation after inverting; independence of the witness makes this the exchange used in $z^p$; $(B^e_{RL})^{-1}$ exists by [thm-cbc-finite-torsion]; the natural $\kappa$ is [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback].

source.place: Actual-adjoint comparison and final base-change sentences; explicit counit-transpose calculation.

proof.text:
Rearrange Step 5 as $l_L^{-1}z^pP'(Q)=C_{Y'}(z^e)a'_{tRL}$ and apply $\Psi'$ with source $C_{X'}tRL$ and target $C_{Y'}sL$. Naturality in source and target [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] identifies the transpose of the left side with
$$H'(l_L^{-1})\circ\beta^p_{C_YL}\circ Q.$$
Step 2 with primes identifies the transpose of the right side with $h_{f',sL}\circ C_{X'}(\beta^e_L)$: by [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], $\beta^e_L$ is exactly the ordinary transpose of $z^e$, and $\beta^p_{C_YL}$ is the stipulated relative transpose of $z^p$. Multiply the resulting equality on the left by $h_{f',sL}^{-1}$ and on the right by $Q^{-1}=v_L$. Since $w_L=h_{f',sL}^{-1}H'(l_L^{-1})$, this proves
$$w_L\circ\beta^p_{C_YL}=C_{X'}(\beta^e_L)\circ v_L.$$
This calculation compares the specified maps, without using an isomorphism between the mates.

source.place: Actual-adjoint comparison and final base-change sentences; explicit counit-transpose calculation.

proof.text: For a morphism $a:L\to M$, naturality of the etale counit and $B^e$ gives $s(a)z^e_L=z^e_M F'(tR(a))$. Transposing and using naturality of the ordinary Hom bijection gives $R's(a)\beta^e_L=\beta^e_M tR(a)$. Naturality of $B^e$ in its input is [thm-cbc-finite-torsion]. Naturality of $B^p$ on witnessed inputs follows from its formula in the statement: for an etale map $G_0\to G$ the factors $S^c,T^c$ are natural by naturality of $\kappa$ and of the comparison of [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison], and $C_{Y'}(B^e)$ by [thm-cbc-finite-torsion]; a map between witnessed inputs comes from a unique etale map by full faithfulness [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], and witness independence [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale] reduces to that case. The same argument uses naturality of $\Psi$ to obtain $E_N P(Hb)=bE_{N_0}$ for a map $b:N_0\to N$, then naturality of $B^p$ and $\Psi'$ gives $H'(Sb)\beta^p_{N_0}=\beta^p_N T(Hb)$ whenever these sources are witnessed. Apply this with $b=C_Y(a)$. The units defining $h$, their inverses, and $\kappa$ are natural as well. Therefore the equality of Step 6 is an equality of natural transformations in $L$. The Hom naturality is [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] and [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]; naturality of $\kappa$ is [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback].

source.place: Actual-adjoint comparison and final base-change sentences; explicit counit-transpose calculation.

proof.text:
Finally let $\alpha:C_YL\xrightarrow{\sim}N$ be replacement of the input by an isomorphic witnessed object. Its exceptional source remains witnessed by $H(\alpha)h_{f,L}$. The source naturality of the Hom bijections and their independence of witnesses [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class], and independence of transported exchange [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale], give the naturality equation proved in Step 7:
$$\beta^p_N\circ TH(\alpha)=H'S(\alpha)\circ\beta^p_{C_YL}.$$
The transported endpoints are $v^N=v_L(TH\alpha)^{-1}$ and $w^N=w_L(H'S\alpha)^{-1}$. Substitution in Step 6 gives $w^N\beta^p_N=C_{X'}(\beta^e_L)v^N$. Thus the equality survives the replacement; there is no choice of a new normalization after changing a witness.
